terms.title: Terms of Service
terms.lead: These terms govern your organization's use of Calibre, a service for running psychological assessments of employees and candidates. Please read them before you create an organization or buy a plan.

about.title: About these terms
body: Calibre is provided by [Company legal name], a company registered at [Registered address] (“Calibre”, “we”, “us”). These Terms of Service (“Terms”) are an agreement between Calibre and the organization that creates a Calibre workspace or buys a plan (the “Customer”, “you”).

By creating an organization, accepting an invitation as its owner or completing a purchase, you accept these Terms on behalf of the Customer and confirm that you are authorised to do so. If you do not have that authority, do not use the service on the Customer’s behalf.

The Data Processing Addendum at /legal/dpa forms part of these Terms. If you sign an order form with us, it takes precedence over these Terms where they conflict; the Data Processing Addendum takes precedence over both on matters of personal data.

accounts.title: Accounts and organizations
body: Each Customer works in its own organization. The person who creates it becomes its owner and can invite colleagues and assign them roles: owner, administrator, psychologist, manager, member or candidate. Roles decide what each person can see and do.

You are responsible for everything done under your organization’s accounts, for choosing who is invited and with which role, and for keeping passwords confidential. Tell us promptly at [security@calibre.example] if you believe an account has been used without authorisation.
Staff accounts must belong to real, identifiable people. Accounts may not be shared.

data.title: Your data and respondents’ data
body: “Customer Data” means everything you and the people you invite put into the service: profiles, answers, scores, reports, conclusions, instruments you upload and settings.

You remain the owner of Customer Data and the controller of the personal data in it. Calibre processes that personal data only on your behalf and on your instructions, as set out in the Data Processing Addendum.

You are responsible for having a lawful basis to assess each respondent, for giving them the information the law requires and for obtaining any consent that is needed. Before a respondent answers for the first time, the service shows them your organization’s privacy notice and asks them to agree; you should set a privacy contact in your settings so they know whom to ask.

responsibleUse.title: Responsible use of assessments
body: Psychological assessments affect people’s careers and wellbeing. When you use Calibre you agree that:

assessment results are never the sole basis for a decision to hire, reject, dismiss, promote, discipline or change the pay of a person; a qualified human reviews the results together with other information before any such decision is made;

clinical and wellbeing screens, which Calibre marks as sensitive, are administered and interpreted only by qualified psychologists. The service shows sensitive instruments and their results only to the organization’s owner and to people with the psychologist role, and you assign that role only to people who hold the relevant qualification;
results are aids to professional judgement and are not a medical or psychiatric diagnosis;
you tell respondents why they are being assessed, that taking part is voluntary where the law requires it to be, and how their results will be used;
you comply with employment, equal-treatment and anti-discrimination law, and you do not use assessments to infer or act on characteristics that the law protects;
you hold every right and licence needed for instruments you upload, including copyrighted tests and their scoring keys.

acceptableUse.title: Acceptable use
body: You must not, and must not let anyone else:
use the service in breach of any law or to harass, deceive or discriminate against anyone;
access or try to access another organization’s data, or test the security of the service other than as described on our security page;
interfere with or overload the service, or circumvent plan limits, access controls or rate limits;
copy, resell or provide the service to third parties, or use it to build a competing product;
upload malware or content you have no right to use.
We may suspend access that breaches this section, as described under “Term, suspension and termination”.

plans.title: Plans and respondent limits
body: Calibre is offered on the Free, Team, Business and Enterprise plans. Each plan includes a number of respondents per subscription year: 25 on Free, 250 on Team, 1,500 on Business, and unlimited on Enterprise, as well as a number of staff seats. The features of each plan are described on our pricing page.
A respondent is a person who submits at least one assessment during the subscription year. Each person counts once per year, however many assessments they take. Respondents never use a staff seat.
When your organization reaches its limit, new respondents cannot submit assessments until you upgrade or the next subscription year starts. Results you already have remain available.

billing.title: Billing through Paddle
body: Our order process is conducted by our online reseller Paddle.com. Paddle.com is the Merchant of Record for all our orders. Paddle provides all customer service inquiries and handles returns.

When you buy a plan you buy it from Paddle, and Paddle’s Buyer Terms apply to the purchase. Paddle collects payment, issues invoices and receipts, and calculates and collects sales tax or VAT. Calibre never receives your full card details.
Prices are shown at checkout, together with any tax. Enterprise plans may be invoiced on terms agreed in an order form, still through Paddle unless the order form says otherwise.

trial.title: Free trial
body: A new organization can try the Business plan free for 14 days. No payment card is needed to start the trial, and nothing is charged when it ends.
When the trial ends, the organization moves to the Free plan unless you have bought a paid plan. Your data is kept, but the Free plan’s features and respondent limit apply from then on.
Each organization can have one trial. We may end trials that are used to get around plan limits.

renewal.title: Renewal and cancellation
body: Paid plans are billed monthly or annually in advance and renew automatically for the same period unless cancelled before the end of the current one.

The owner can cancel at any time from the organization’s billing settings or through the links in Paddle’s receipt emails. Cancellation takes effect at the end of the period already paid for; the organization then moves to the Free plan.
Upgrades take effect immediately, and Paddle charges the prorated difference. Downgrades take effect at the next renewal.

We may change prices for future periods by giving at least 30 days’ notice by email to the organization’s owner. The new price applies from the first renewal after the notice period. Refunds are covered by our refund policy at /legal/refunds.

service.title: Changes to the service and support
body: We work to keep the service available and secure, and we may carry out maintenance that briefly interrupts it. We will try to schedule planned maintenance outside normal working hours.
We improve the service continually and may change or remove features. We will not materially reduce the core functionality of a paid plan during a period you have already paid for.
Support is provided by email at [support@calibre.example].

ip.title: Intellectual property
body: Calibre and its licensors own the service, including its software, design and the instruments in its library. We grant you a non-exclusive, non-transferable right to use the service for your internal purposes during your subscription.
You own Customer Data, including instruments you upload. You grant us the rights we need to host, process and display it in order to provide the service to you.
If you send us suggestions, we may use them without any obligation to you.

confidentiality.title: Confidentiality
body: Each party will keep the other’s non-public information confidential, use it only to perform these Terms and disclose it only to people who need to know it and are bound by similar obligations. This does not apply to information that is or becomes public through no fault of the receiving party, or that the law requires to be disclosed.

warranties.title: Warranties and disclaimers
body: We will provide the service with reasonable skill and care and in line with the Data Processing Addendum.

Apart from that, and to the extent the law allows, the service is provided “as is”. We do not guarantee that any assessment predicts job performance or any other outcome, or that the service will be uninterrupted or error-free. You are responsible for the decisions you make using it.

liability.title: Limitation of liability
body: Neither party is liable for any loss of profits, revenue, business or goodwill, or for any indirect or consequential loss.

Each party’s total liability arising out of or in connection with these Terms in any 12-month period is limited to the fees the Customer paid for the service in the 12 months before the event giving rise to the claim. For organizations on the Free plan, it is limited to [Free plan liability cap].
These limits do not apply to liability that cannot be limited by law, to fraud, or to a Customer’s obligation to pay fees.

termination.title: Term, suspension and termination
body: These Terms apply from the moment you accept them until your organization is deleted.
You can stop using the service at any time. The owner can delete the organization from its settings; this cannot be undone.

We may suspend access, with notice where practical, if it is needed to protect the service or other customers, if fees are overdue, or if these Terms are seriously breached. Either party may terminate these Terms if the other materially breaches them and does not fix the breach within 30 days of written notice.
Sections on data, intellectual property, confidentiality, liability and governing law survive termination.

export.title: Data export and deletion
body: While your organization exists you can print or save reports and, on plans that include it, export analytics as CSV. Each person can download a copy of their own data from their account page.

When the owner deletes the organization, its results, reports, conclusions, audit events and uploaded instruments are deleted from the live database at once. Copies in backups are overwritten within [backup retention period]. Personal accounts of people who also belong to other organizations are kept for those organizations.
If we terminate these Terms for a reason other than your breach, we will give you at least 30 days to export your data before we delete it.

law.title: Governing law and disputes
body: These Terms and any dispute arising from them are governed by the laws of [Governing law jurisdiction]. The courts of [Courts / venue] have exclusive jurisdiction, unless mandatory law gives you the right to bring a claim elsewhere.
Before starting proceedings, each party will try in good faith to settle the dispute by talking to the other for at least 30 days.

changes.title: Changes to these terms
body: We may update these Terms. For material changes we will give at least 30 days’ notice by email to organization owners and on this page. If you do not agree, you may cancel before the change takes effect. The version number and date at the top of this page show which version is current.

contact.title: Contact
body: [Company legal name], [Registered address]. Legal questions: [legal@calibre.example]. Support: [support@calibre.example].

dpa.title: Data Processing Addendum
dpa.lead: This addendum sets out how Calibre processes personal data on behalf of the organizations that use it, as required by Article 28 of the GDPR and equivalent laws.

scope.title: Scope and roles
body: This Data Processing Addendum (“DPA”) forms part of the Terms of Service between [Company legal name] (“Calibre”) and the Customer. It applies whenever Calibre processes personal data contained in Customer Data (“Customer Personal Data”).

The Customer is the controller of Customer Personal Data and Calibre is its processor. Where the Customer itself acts as a processor for another controller, Calibre is its subprocessor, and the Customer is responsible for passing on the instructions of that controller.

“Data Protection Law” means the EU General Data Protection Regulation (“GDPR”), the UK GDPR and Data Protection Act 2018, the Swiss Federal Act on Data Protection, and any other data protection law that applies to the processing. Terms such as “personal data”, “processing” and “personal data breach” have the meanings given in the GDPR.

subject.title: Subject matter, duration, nature and purpose
body: Subject matter: hosting and processing of Customer Personal Data so that the Customer can run psychological assessments of its employees and candidates and review the results.
Duration: the term of the Terms of Service, plus the period needed to delete the data as described in section “Deletion and return of data”.

Nature: collection through the service, storage, scoring and interpretation of answers, generation of reports and analytics, sending of transactional email, access control and audit logging, export and deletion.
Purpose: providing the service to the Customer under the Terms of Service and the Customer’s documented instructions.

dataSubjects.title: Data subjects
body: the Customer’s employees and other workers who take assessments;
candidates invited to hiring rounds;
the Customer’s staff who use the dashboard: owners, administrators, psychologists and managers.

categories.title: Categories of personal data
body: identity and contact details: name, email address, phone number, date of birth and, if added, a photo;
work details: team, position, manager and other profile fields the Customer defines;
assessment data: answers, the scores and interpretations calculated from them, reports, and conclusions written by the Customer’s psychologists;
consent records: when a respondent agreed to the Customer’s privacy notice or withdrew their agreement;
account and security data: a hash of the password, session records and the audit log of who opened or changed personal data and when.

specialCategories.title: Special categories of data
body: Clinical and wellbeing screens, such as questionnaires on anxiety, depression or burnout, can reveal data concerning health, which is a special category of personal data under Article 9 of the GDPR.

The Customer decides whether to use such instruments and is responsible for having a valid condition for processing under Article 9(2) and any local law. Calibre marks these instruments as sensitive and shows them and their results only to the organization’s owner and to people with the psychologist role.

instructions.title: Processing on instructions
body: Calibre processes Customer Personal Data only on the Customer’s documented instructions, which are the Terms of Service, this DPA and the Customer’s use and configuration of the service, unless the law requires otherwise. In that case Calibre will inform the Customer before processing, unless the law prohibits it.
Calibre will tell the Customer promptly if it believes an instruction infringes Data Protection Law.

personnel.title: Confidentiality of personnel
body: Calibre ensures that everyone authorised to process Customer Personal Data is bound by confidentiality and accesses it only as far as is needed to provide, support or secure the service.

security.title: Security measures
body: Calibre implements appropriate technical and organisational measures under Article 32 of the GDPR, including:
separation of each Customer’s data into its own organization, with membership checked on the server for every page and action;
role-based access control, with individual results limited to owners, administrators and psychologists, and sensitive results limited to owners and psychologists;
passwords stored only as bcrypt hashes; invitation, password-reset and assessment links stored only as SHA-256 hashes and made to expire;
sessions held on the server and identified by an HTTP-only cookie that is sent only over HTTPS in production;
rate limits on sign-in, sign-up and password reset;
an audit log of access to individual results and changes to people, roles and settings, kept for 24 months;
retention settings that automatically delete results and candidates’ data after the period the Customer chooses;
encryption in transit using TLS, and encryption at rest provided by [Hosting provider] — [confirm with hosting provider];
backups kept for [backup retention period] — [confirm backup policy].
Calibre may update these measures as long as the overall level of protection is not reduced. The current measures are described on our security page.

subprocessors.title: Subprocessors
body: The Customer gives Calibre general authorisation to engage subprocessors. The current list is published at /legal/subprocessors.

Calibre will notify the Customer at least 30 days before adding or replacing a subprocessor, by email to the organization’s owner or to subscribers of the list. The Customer may object on reasonable data-protection grounds within that period; if the parties cannot resolve the objection, the Customer may terminate the affected service and receive a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees for the unused period.
Calibre imposes data protection obligations on each subprocessor that are no less protective than this DPA and remains responsible to the Customer for their performance.

transfers.title: International transfers
body: Customer Personal Data is hosted in [Hosting provider, region]. Calibre or its subprocessors may process it in other countries listed on the subprocessors page.

Where Customer Personal Data is transferred from the European Economic Area, the United Kingdom or Switzerland to a country that does not have an adequacy decision, the parties rely on the Standard Contractual Clauses approved by Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2021/914 (“SCCs”), which are incorporated into this DPA by reference: Module 2 (controller to processor) where the Customer is a controller, and Module 3 (processor to processor) where it is a processor. For the United Kingdom, the International Data Transfer Addendum issued by the Information Commissioner applies; for Switzerland, the SCCs apply with the references adapted to Swiss law.

For the purposes of the SCCs: the optional docking clause applies; option 2 (general authorisation) applies under clause 9 with the notice period set out above; the optional wording in clause 11 does not apply; clauses 17 and 18 are governed by the law and courts of [EU member state]; and the annexes are completed by sections 2 to 5 and 8 of this DPA. Calibre ensures that its subprocessors’ transfers are covered by the SCCs or another valid transfer mechanism.

requests.title: Assistance with data subject requests
body: The service lets the Customer respond to most requests itself: each person can download a copy of their data and withdraw their consent from their account page, and administrators can correct profiles or remove a person, which erases that person’s answers, results and reports in the organization.

If Calibre receives a request directly from a data subject, it will pass it to the Customer without undue delay and will not answer it except on the Customer’s instructions. Calibre will otherwise provide reasonable assistance, taking into account the nature of the processing.

breach.title: Personal data breaches
body: Calibre will notify the Customer without undue delay, and in any event within 72 hours, after becoming aware of a personal data breach affecting Customer Personal Data.

The notice will describe, as far as is known at the time, the nature of the breach, the categories and approximate number of data subjects and records concerned, its likely consequences, and the measures taken or proposed to address it. Calibre will provide further information as it becomes available and will take reasonable steps to contain the breach and limit its effects.
Notification is not an admission of fault or liability.

assistance.title: Impact assessments and consultation
body: Taking into account the nature of the processing and the information available to it, Calibre will provide reasonable assistance to the Customer with data protection impact assessments and prior consultations with supervisory authorities that relate to the service.

deletion.title: Deletion and return of data
body: During the term, the Customer can export its data as described in the Terms of Service. Results and candidates’ data are also deleted automatically according to the retention periods the Customer sets in its privacy settings, and audit events are deleted after 24 months.

When the organization is deleted, or at the end of the term, Calibre deletes Customer Personal Data from its live systems, and from backups within [backup retention period], unless the law requires Calibre to keep it.

audits.title: Information and audits
body: Calibre will make available the information reasonably necessary to demonstrate compliance with this DPA and Article 28 of the GDPR.

The Customer, or an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, may audit Calibre’s compliance once a year with at least 30 days’ written notice, during business hours and at the Customer’s expense, or more often if a supervisory authority requires it or after a personal data breach. Calibre may answer an audit request with existing third-party audit reports if it holds them.

general.title: Liability and precedence
body: Each party’s liability under this DPA is subject to the limitations in the Terms of Service, except where Data Protection Law does not allow it.
If this DPA conflicts with the Terms of Service, this DPA prevails. If it conflicts with the SCCs, the SCCs prevail.

contact.title: Contact
body: Questions about this DPA or requests for a countersigned copy: [privacy@calibre.example]. Data protection officer or EU/UK representative, if appointed: [DPO / representative details].

subprocessors.title: Subprocessors
subprocessors.lead: The third parties that Calibre uses to provide the service and that may process personal data on behalf of our customers.

about.title: About this list
body: A subprocessor is a company that Calibre engages to process personal data that our customers entrust to us. Each one is bound by a written agreement that protects the data at least as well as our Data Processing Addendum.
Paddle is included for completeness. As merchant of record it sells the subscription and acts as an independent controller of billing details; it does not receive respondents’ answers or results.

changes.title: Changes to this list
body: We notify customers at least 30 days before adding or replacing a subprocessor, by email to organization owners. To be notified as well, write to [privacy@calibre.example]. Customers can object to a change as described in the Data Processing Addendum.

refunds.title: Refund policy
refunds.lead: When you can get a refund for a Calibre subscription and how to ask for one. Payments and refunds are handled by Paddle, our merchant of record.

paddle.title: Who handles refunds
body: Our order process is conducted by our online reseller Paddle.com. Paddle.com is the Merchant of Record for all our orders. Paddle provides all customer service inquiries and handles returns.
Refunds are paid by Paddle to the original payment method, in the currency you paid in, and are subject to Paddle’s Buyer Terms as well as this policy.

window.title: 14-day refund on your first purchase
body: If Calibre is not right for your organization, you can ask for a full refund within 14 days of your first payment for a Team or Business plan, whether monthly or annual. No reason is needed.
This applies once per organization. When the refund is issued, the subscription is cancelled and the organization moves to the Free plan; your data is kept.

renewals.title: Renewals
body: Subscriptions renew automatically. You can cancel at any time before the renewal date in your organization’s billing settings, and you will not be charged again.

Renewal payments are generally not refundable. If you forgot to cancel and no assessments have been submitted since the renewal, contact us within 14 days of the renewal date and we will look at your request case by case.

changes.title: Upgrades, downgrades and cancellation
body: When you upgrade, Paddle charges only the prorated difference for the rest of the period. Downgrades and cancellations take effect at the end of the period you have paid for, and unused time is not refunded.

exceptions.title: When refunds are not given
body: requests made more than 14 days after the payment, except as described under “Renewals”;
accounts suspended or terminated for breach of our Terms of Service;
repeated purchases and refunds that appear to abuse this policy;
Enterprise agreements, where the refund terms of the order form apply.

trial.title: Free trial and Free plan
body: The 14-day Business trial needs no payment card and nothing is charged when it ends, so there is nothing to refund. The Free plan is free.

request.title: How to request a refund
body: Reply to the receipt email Paddle sent you, or find your order at paddle.net and contact Paddle from there. You can also write to us at [billing@calibre.example] with your order number and your organization’s name, and we will ask Paddle to process it.
Once approved, refunds usually reach your account within 5 to 10 business days, depending on your bank or card provider.

rights.title: Your statutory rights
body: Calibre is a business service, sold to organizations rather than to consumers. Nothing in this policy limits any right you have under law that cannot be excluded.

security.title: Security at Calibre
security.lead: Assessment results are among the most sensitive data an HR team holds. This page describes the protections built into Calibre today and lists separately what is not yet in place.

tenancy.title: Each organization is kept separate
body: Every customer works in its own organization, and every dashboard address includes it, for example /acme/people. On each page and action the server checks that the signed-in person is a member of that organization and has a role that allows what they are doing. A person who belongs to several organizations sees only the data of the one they are working in.

roles.title: Roles and least privilege
body: Access is based on six roles: owner, administrator, psychologist, manager, member and candidate.
Individual answers and scores are visible only to owners, administrators and psychologists. Managers see team averages, not individual results.
Members only take assessments; candidates see nothing but the hiring round they were invited to.
Nobody can grant a role higher than their own, and only an owner can make someone an owner.
Only the owner can read the audit log.

sensitive.title: Clinical and wellbeing screens
body: Instruments that can reveal health information are marked as sensitive. The service shows them, and their results, only to the owner and to people with the psychologist role. Other staff do not see them in the library, in reports or in analytics. We ask customers to assign the psychologist role only to qualified psychologists.

respondents.title: Respondent links and consent
body: Respondents do not need a password. Each one gets a personal link by email, which contains a random 256-bit token; only its SHA-256 hash is stored. The link expires and stops working once the assessment is completed or the round is closed. Opening it signs in only that person and ends any other session in the same browser.

Before answering for the first time, a respondent sees the organization’s privacy notice and must agree to it. They can later download a copy of their data or withdraw their consent from their account page.

accounts.title: Passwords and sessions
body: Passwords are stored only as bcrypt hashes.
Password-reset links are single-use, expire after 60 minutes and are stored only as hashes. Resetting a password signs out every other session.
Sessions are stored on the server and identified by an HTTP-only cookie that is sent only over HTTPS in production. A session ends after a day without activity.
Sign-in, sign-up and password reset are rate-limited to slow down password guessing.

audit.title: Audit log
body: The audit log records who opened an individual result or report, changes to people, roles and follow-up flags, ownership transfers, settings changes, personal data exports, consent withdrawals, retention clean-ups and published instruments. It stores identifiers only, never answers or scores, and events are kept for 24 months.
The audit log is included in the Business and Enterprise plans.

retention.title: Retention and deletion
body: Each organization chooses how long results are kept (6, 12, 24, 36 or 60 months, or until deleted by hand) and how long candidates’ data is kept after their round closes (3, 6 or 12 months, or until deleted by hand). A scheduled job deletes data past these periods every hour.

Removing a person from an organization erases their answers, results, reports and drafts there. The owner can delete the whole organization, which removes all of its results, reports, instruments and audit events.

indexing.title: Private pages stay out of search engines
body: Dashboard pages, invitations and personal links are sent with a noindex, nofollow header, so search engines do not list them.

infrastructure.title: Hosting and encryption
body: Calibre is hosted by [Hosting provider, region]. Traffic is encrypted in transit with TLS. Data at rest is encrypted by [Hosting provider] — [confirm]. Backups are taken [backup frequency] and kept for [backup retention period] — [confirm].
Email is sent through Resend, and payments are handled by Paddle. The full list is on our subprocessors page.

roadmap.title: Not yet in place
body: To be clear about what Calibre does not offer today, the following are on the roadmap and not yet available:
single sign-on (SAML or OpenID Connect);
two-factor authentication for staff accounts;
an independent penetration test;
SOC 2 or ISO 27001 certification.

report.title: Report a vulnerability
body: If you believe you have found a security issue, please email [security@calibre.example] with a description and the steps to reproduce it. We will acknowledge your report within [response time].

Please do not access or change other people’s data, do not degrade the service, and give us reasonable time to fix the issue before disclosing it. We will not take legal action against research carried out in good faith within these rules.
